newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan signs gas memorandum with Iran, Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan signs gas memorandum with Iran, Turkey.

text.p: The Presidents of Turkmenistan, Turkey and Iran signed a memorandum on Wednesday to export up to 30 billion cubic metres (bcm) of Turkmen natural gas annually to Turkey via Iran.
"We have signed a gas deal this morning," Turkish President Suleyman Demirel told Reuters after the signing.
Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov also signed the memorandum in the Turkmen capital.
Details of the deal were scarce, but officials present at the signing said that the memorandum envisaged exporting up to 30 bcm a year to Turkey.
The gas could be pumped from the huge Dauletabad gas field in the south east of Turkmenistan, they said.
It was unclear how this might affect plans United States oil company Unocal Corp has to build a gas pipeline from the Turkmen border across Afghanistan to Pakistan, and possibly on to India.
The $2.5-billion-dollar plan envisages exporting gas from the Dauletabad field.
"As the gas might come from Dauletabad, this poses a lot of questions for the trans-Afghan pipeline," a Western diplomat said.
Turkmenistan is keen to forge gas export deals with its neighbours and with foreign oil companies.

It is sitting on enormous gas reserves, but limited export capabilities and the lack of cash to build new ones are frustrating its plans to become the next Kuwait. Average wages in the former Soviet Central Asian state are under $20 a month.
Natural gas output is targeted at 53 bcm in 1997, up sharply from 35 bcm last year. Exports are pegged at 40 bcm, half of which is due to reach hard-currency markets in Western Europe.

Officials have said that Turkmenistan would be capable of producing up to 100 bcm annually if export outlets could be found. Turkmenistan relies heavily on Russian pipelines leading to Western Europe and owned by gas monpoly Gazprom.
Estimated gas reserves are 21 trillion cubic metres.
